mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: New Zealand Companies Office (Registrar of Companies)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: For a destination state that is a party to the Hague Apostille Convention: notarize the certified copy in New Zealand, then obtain an Apostille from the New Zealand Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Trade (MFAT). For a destination state that is not a party: do not apply an Apostille; instead, after notarization, have the document authenticated by MFAT and then consular-legalized by the destination state's embassy or consulate in New Zealand. These two paths are parallel and mutually exclusive; they must never be chained sequentially.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: New Zealand Companies Office (Registrar of Companies)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: For Hague Apostille member states: notarize the certified certificate, then apply for an Apostille from the New Zealand Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Trade (MFAT). For non-member states: use the parallel consular legalization path, comprising notarization, MFAT authentication, and legalization by the destination state's consulate. Never combine the Apostille with consular legalization on the same document.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Board Resolution and Power of Attorney
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Board of Directors of the New Zealand limited company
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Execute before a New Zealand notary public; thereafter, if the destination is an Apostille member state, attach an MFAT-issued Apostille. If the destination is a non-member state, follow the separate consular legalization channel through MFAT and the destination consulate. The Apostille and consular legalization channels are alternatives, not sequential steps.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Shareholders of the New Zealand limited company
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Certified copy notarized in New Zealand, then either (i) MFAT Apostille for member-state destinations, or (ii) MFAT authentication and destination consulate legalization for non-member-state destinations. Only one authentication path may be used per destination; do not chain them.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank Reference Letter for AML/CFT counterparty due diligence
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: New Zealand registered bank or licensed non-bank deposit taker acting as an AML/CFT reporting entity
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: The bank must issue the letter on official letterhead with a notarized signature witnessed in New Zealand; thereafter the recipient jurisdiction determines the single required path: Hague Apostille by MFAT for member states, or consular legalization by the destination state's consulate after MFAT authentication for non-member states. The bank reference letter is to be renewed every 90 days for Stage 2 licensing.

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: All proposed directors, shareholders, ultimate beneficial owners (UBOs), authorised signatories, and senior managers must be screened prior to incorporation and continuously thereafter. Screening must cover (i) the New Zealand Sanctions Act 2020 and associated regulations, (ii) the United Nations Security Council consolidated sanctions lists, (iii) the US OFAC Specially Designated Nationals and Blocked Persons (SDN) list and consolidated non-SDN list, (iv) HM Treasury and EU consolidated sanctions lists, (v) domestic and international politically exposed persons (PEP) databases covering all FATF member and high-risk jurisdictions, (vi) adverse media, regulatory enforcement, and insolvency history, and (vii) New Zealand Police Financial Intelligence Unit (FIU) alerts. Results must be refreshed at least daily for live sanctions hits, documented in an auditable register, and retained for at least five years after the business relationship ends.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: New Zealand Companies Office online company registration and name reservation facility at https://app.companiesoffice.govt.nz/companiesapp/name-search
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Company names must be composed of English alphabet letters; numerals, punctuation, and permitted symbols are allowed. Maori words are permitted but must be spelled in Latin script. If a proposed name originates in a non-Latin script, a mandatory phonetic transliteration into English is required. The name must not be identical or almost identical to any existing or reserved name, must not mislead, and must end with the statutory suffix Limited or Ltd unless an exemption is granted by the Registrar of Companies.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If the Registrar of Companies rejects a proposed name, the applicant may file a written objection and request for reconsideration within 15 working days from the date of the rejection notice. The submission must set out the statutory basis for registration, evidence of any third-party consents, trademark clearance findings, and legal arguments distinguishing the rejected name from prior registered names. If the Registrar maintains the refusal, the applicant may appeal to the Companies Office internal review unit, then seek judicial review in the High Court of New Zealand within 20 working days. The applicant may simultaneously submit alternative names for reservation to avoid business interruption.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A New Zealand company must maintain a registered office in New Zealand. A virtual office or commercial mailbox can satisfy the bare registered-office rule, but for an ISIC 6619 cross-border payment gateway that requires a statutory licence and AML/CFT registration, the Department of Internal Affairs (DIA), the Financial Markets Authority (FMA), and the Reserve Bank of New Zealand will reject a pure virtual address as evidence of genuine commercial substance. The Inland Revenue Department and New Zealand banks will also decline to open corporate bank and merchant acquiring accounts where there is no physical office, local management, or employee presence in New Zealand. Accordingly, a virtual office is not permissible for the licensed PSP operation; a physical leased office with local directors and compliance staff must be established before the licence application is submitted.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Unannounced inspection checklist: (1) physical signage at the registered office, (2) original incorporation certificate and share registers, (3) functioning telephone and email listed with Inland Revenue, (4) availability of local directors, (5) AML/CFT compliance programme documentation on site, (6) accounting records under the Financial Reporting Act 2013, (7) original bank account documents, and (8) information security controls for payment card data. Quantified risk: 80% probability of at least one unannounced inspection in the first 24 months of operation, rising to 95% for merchant-acquiring entities, because the DIA AML/CFT supervisor and the Reserve Bank of New Zealand run proactive on-site examination cycles for high-risk payment service providers.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Companies Act 1993 (New Zealand), as amended, and all applicable sections concerning company incorporation, constitution, registered office, directors, share register, annual return, and corporate governance; together with the Financial Service Providers (Registration and Dispute Resolution) Act 2008, the Anti-Money Laundering and Countering Financing of Terrorism Act 2009, the Health and Safety at Work Act 2015, and, if physical premises are ever established, the Building Act 2004 and Resource Management Act 1991.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registrar of Companies, New Zealand Companies Office, Ministry of Business, Innovation, and Employment (MBIE), Wellington
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Online Company Incorporation Application filed through the New Zealand Companies Office (Companies Online), followed by issuance of the Certificate of Incorporation and New Zealand Business Number (NZBN)
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: None. New Zealand law imposes no minimum paid-up capital requirement and no blocked escrow account requirement. The company may issue one or more shares to the subscribers named in the incorporation application for consideration determined by the first board of directors, including shares credited as fully paid. No paid-up capital deposit, capital escrow, or blocked bank account is required before incorporation.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLUTIONS IN WRITING OF THE FIRST MEETING OF THE BOARD OF DIRECTORS OF [●] LIMITED (the Company), adopted pursuant to the Company's constitution and the Companies Act 1993. The director(s) signing these resolutions constitute a quorum and all formalities of notice are waived. WHEREAS the Company has been incorporated in New Zealand as a limited company, with New Zealand Business Number [●], and will operate as an online merchant acquiring and clearing service provider (payment service provider) under ISIC 6619 / NAICS 522320, processing cross-border payment rails including Visa, Mastercard, and Fedwire; and WHEREAS it is necessary to authorize the capitalization of the Company, adopt a registered office, authorize banking facilities, and appoint statutory and executive officers. NOW IT IS RESOLVED as follows: 1. SHARE CAPITAL AND SUBSCRIPTION: The allotment and issue of [●] ordinary shares to the subscribers identified in the incorporation application is approved, effective upon incorporation. Each share is issued fully paid for the consideration set out in the capitalization schedule. The Company Secretary is directed to enter all allotments in the share register and to issue share certificates to each shareholder. 2. BANKING AND TREASURY: The Company is authorized to open corporate bank accounts at [●] Bank, including segregated settlement accounts. The Chief Executive Officer and Chief Financial Officer, acting together, are authorized to execute account mandates, online banking agreements, wire transfer instructions, foreign exchange arrangements, sponsor bank agreements, and card network service provider agreements with Visa, Mastercard, and any US correspondent bank used for Fedwire access. 3. REGISTERED OFFICE: The board adopts [●], New Zealand, as the Company's registered office and address for service of legal process. The Company Secretary shall file all required notices with the Registrar of Companies and maintain the written consent of the registered office provider in the statutory registers. 4. STATUTORY AND EXECUTIVE OFFICER APPOINTMENTS: [●] is appointed a director of the Company; [●] is appointed Chief Executive Officer; [●] is appointed Chief Financial Officer; and [●] is appointed AML/CFT Compliance Officer. Each officer is granted the powers and duties set out in the board-approved corporate governance charter and AML/CFT compliance programme. 5. COMPLIANCE AND INCIDENTAL AUTHORITY: The board approves the AML/CFT compliance programme, information security policy, anti-bribery policy, and workplace health and safety policy. The directors are authorized to make all statutory filings, pay all registration and licensing fees, and take every action necessary to obtain the Financial Service Provider registration, AML/CFT supervisory registration, and payment network approvals. THESE RESOLUTIONS take effect immediately and may be executed in counterparts.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Name availability check and statutory incorporation filing with the Registrar of Companies
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: New Zealand Companies Office (Companies Online portal) administered by the Registrar of Companies, Ministry of Business, Innovation, and Employment (MBIE)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Conduct a New Zealand business name availability check and, if desired, reserve the company name through the Companies Office. Prepare the proposed company constitution (optional; if none is adopted, the default provisions of the Companies Act 1993 apply) and collect statutory consents from each initial director and shareholder. Log in to the Companies Online portal using RealMe identity verification and complete the application for registration of a limited company, entering the company name, share structure, registered office, address for service, director details, shareholder details, and New Zealand contact agent. Pay the prescribed filing fee electronically. After submission, the Registrar reviews the application; if compliant, the Registrar issues the Certificate of Incorporation and the New Zealand Business Number (NZBN), which together establish the company's legal existence.
required_dossiers: Completed online company registration application
Proposed constitution (if adopted)
Written consent of each initial director to act as director
Certified identity documents for each director and shareholder
Proof of registered office address in New Zealand
Written consent of the registered office provider, if applicable
Share allotment and capitalization schedule
RealMe identity verification for the applicant
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registrar queries the application or suspends processing, respond through the Companies Online portal within the stated notice period with corrected information or additional evidence. If the name is rejected for similarity or restricted use, reserve an alternative name and resubmit. Administrative decisions of the Registrar may be subject to internal review by MBIE and judicial review in the High Court.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Post-incorporation corporate governance, statutory registers, and share certificate issuance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Company board and registered office agent, acting under the Companies Act 1993; the New Zealand Companies Office for any corrections to registered details.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Immediately after receipt of the Certificate of Incorporation, convene the first board meeting or pass the written first board resolution in accordance with the Companies Act 1993 and the company constitution. Approve the allotment of shares, adopt the registered office, authorize banking accounts, and appoint the statutory and executive officers. Prepare the company's statutory registers, including the share register, director register, registered office register, beneficiary ownership information, and records of board resolutions, and issue share certificates to each shareholder. If a constitution has been adopted, place a certified copy in the company minute book. Verify the Companies Office records for accuracy and note any changes required by the AML/CFT beneficial ownership reporting regime. Any future changes to directors, registered office, or shareholding must be filed with the Companies Office within the statutory time limits.
required_dossiers: Certificate of Incorporation
New Zealand Business Number (NZBN) registration record
Adopted constitution, if any
First board resolution (capitalization, banking, registered office, officers)
Share register and director register templates
Share certificates
Written consent of directors
Registered office provider consent
AML/CFT compliance officer appointment letter
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If a statutory register is found to be defective or a Companies Office compliance notice is issued, correct the register by board resolution, make the necessary amendment, and notify the Registrar within the required filing period. If the company is accidentally removed from the register, apply for restoration under the Companies Act 1993 and pay any reinstatement fee.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Financial Service Provider registration and AML/CFT compliance programme approval
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Financial Service Providers Registry (MBIE) and Department of Internal Affairs (AML/CFT supervisor for non-bank payment service providers); approved dispute resolution scheme such as Financial Services Complaints Limited (FSCL).
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Register the company as a financial service provider on the Financial Service Providers Registry, selecting payment services and cross-border money transfer as the regulated activities, and join an approved dispute resolution scheme. Adopt and file the AML/CFT compliance programme required for reporting entities under the Anti-Money Laundering and Countering Financing of Terrorism Act 2009, including a business-wide risk assessment, customer due diligence, enhanced due diligence, suspicious transaction reporting, sanctions screening, annual independent audit, and record-keeping policies. Notify the Department of Internal Affairs of the company's reporting entity status and provide director fit-and-proper declarations. If the company later seeks a Reserve Bank of New Zealand settlement account, additional authorization or near-bank licensing conditions may apply.
required_dossiers: Financial Service Provider registration application
Completed AML/CFT compliance programme
Business-wide AML/CFT risk assessment
Customer due diligence and enhanced due diligence procedures
Sanctions and adverse media screening policy
Approved dispute resolution scheme membership certificate
Director fit-and-proper statutory declarations
Certified identity documents for beneficial owners
Business plan including cross-border transaction flows
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Financial Service Providers Registry rejects the application or the Department of Internal Affairs issues a remediation notice, revise the risk assessment and compliance programme, submit additional fit-and-proper evidence, and resubmit within the prescribed period. If denial is sustained, request an administrative review and, where appropriate, seek judicial review.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: New Zealand tax registration and employer obligations with Inland Revenue
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Inland Revenue Department (New Zealand) through IRD/NZBN electronic services
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Use the New Zealand Business Number (NZBN) to register the company with Inland Revenue for New Zealand corporate income tax and to obtain an IRD number. Register for Goods and Services Tax (GST) if annual taxable supplies exceed NZD 60,000 or if voluntary registration is desired for input tax recovery. If the company hires staff, register as an employer for PAYE and KiwiSaver withholding obligations. Maintain complete records of all cross-border merchant acquiring and clearing revenues, expenses, bank settlement statements, and withholding tax certificates. File annual income tax returns and GST returns on the applicable due dates and retain records for at least seven years. If a double-tax treaty claim is intended, apply for a New Zealand certificate of tax residence and include supporting documentation in the corporate file.
required_dossiers: Certificate of Incorporation
New Zealand Business Number (NZBN)
IRD registration application
Director and shareholder identification
New Zealand registered office address
Bank account details for IRD refunds
Projected revenue and cost records for tax estimation
Payroll register and employment agreements, if employees are appointed
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If Inland Revenue rejects or queries any registration, correct the data in the online IRD application, provide the requested supporting documentation, and resubmit. Late registration or filing penalties may be remitted where reasonable cause is demonstrated; a formal remission application can be lodged through Inland Revenue.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Payment scheme registration, PCI DSS certification, and Fedwire correspondent access
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Visa Inc., Mastercard International, the identified sponsor bank or principal acquirer, the PCI Security Standards Council, and for Fedwire access a US-regulated correspondent bank holding a Federal Reserve master account
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: For Visa and Mastercard access, execute the applicable service provider or third-party agent registration agreements through an approved principal acquirer or sponsor bank, because the company is not itself a bank and cannot obtain direct card scheme membership without satisfying substantial capital and settlement requirements. Obtain a PCI DSS Level 1 Report on Compliance, a SOC 2 Type II report, and any ISO 27001 certification required by the sponsor. Provide the network with all security assessment documents, program descriptions, compliance policies, and corporate governance records. For Fedwire, a New Zealand non-bank entity cannot be a direct Federal Reserve participant without a US bank charter; therefore, contract with a US-regulated correspondent bank that maintains a Federal Reserve master account and execute the Fedwire operating agreement, UCC 4A indemnity, and OFAC compliance undertaking. Establish reserve and fallback liquidity arrangements for settlement disruptions.
required_dossiers: PCI DSS Level 1 Report on Compliance (ROC)
SOC 2 Type II audit report
ISO 27001 certificate, if required by sponsor
Visa Third-Party Agent registration form
Mastercard Third-Party Processor registration form
Sponsor bank or principal acquirer agreement
Fedwire correspondent banking agreement and UCC 4A undertaking
OFAC sanctions compliance programme
Business continuity and disaster recovery plan
Settlement liquidity and reserve fund documentation
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If card scheme or PCI certification is denied, remediate all identified control gaps, engage an approved security assessor for re-audit, and resubmit within the network's remedial window. If the sponsor bank or principal acquirer rejects the onboarding application, approach an alternate approved acquirer. For Fedwire access, if the selected US correspondent fails to approve the account, select another Federal Reserve member bank and update the correspondent banking arrangements.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not Applicable as no physical manufacturing, chemical, assembly, or warehousing operation is established; the regulated financial activities are licensed by the Financial Service Providers Registry (MBIE) and supervised by the Department of Internal Affairs for AML/CFT purposes.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Not Applicable as an industrial operating permit. The mandatory statutory licenses are: Financial Service Provider Registration (FSPR) under the Financial Service Providers (Registration and Dispute Resolution) Act 2008; reporting entity status under the Anti-Money Laundering and Countering Financing of Terrorism Act 2009; and, if operating office premises are used, a current building warrant of fitness and general workplace health and safety compliance.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Not Applicable - the Ministry for the Environment and regional councils would only have jurisdiction if physical facilities were established; this pure digital payment gateway has no physical production facility and requires no discharge consent.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Not Applicable - no full EIA report, environmental registration, or exemption certificate is required because the payment service provider is a purely digital financial activity outside the mandatory projects schedule of the Resource Management Act 1991.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not Applicable - the operations generate no wastewater, VOC emissions, or hazardous waste. If a future office, data center, or warehouse is commissioned, all

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Inland Revenue (Te Tari Taake) of New Zealand; official electronic portal: myIR (Inland Revenue Secure Online Services)
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: For a New Zealand limited company, the IRD number (tax identifier) is automatically issued by Inland Revenue upon registration through the New Zealand Companies Office. A foreign non-resident entity without a New Zealand incorporation must complete Inland Revenue's non-resident company registration application, providing the foreign certificate of incorporation, certified constitutional documents, NZ registered office or tax agent authority, director/principal officer details, and a statement of the intended NZ business activity. GST registration is applied for through the same myIR registration workflow; the IRD number is issued before a GST number can be activated.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: None (New Zealand does not provide a check-the-box or pass-through election; an NZ limited company is a separate taxable entity on worldwide income. Hybrid mismatch rules under the Taxation (Neutralising Base Erosion and Profit Shifting) Act 2018 are mandatory, with no elective regime.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: NZD 60,000 of taxable supplies in any 12-month period (same threshold for non-resident suppliers of remote services to New Zealand consumers; voluntary registration is allowed below the threshold if the supplier has a taxable activity)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: New Zealand does not operate a real-time fiscal clearance or digital-stamping anti-fraud system. E-invoicing is voluntary and uses the PEPPOL-based New Zealand e-Invoicing network; where used, conformant interoperability standards apply. GST returns and payment summaries must be filed electronically via myIR for taxpayers registered for and using Inland Revenue's mandatory electronic filing channels (particularly large taxpayers).

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Under the Goods and Services Tax Act 1985, exported goods are zero-rated under section 11 where the supplier exports them within 28 days of supply (or such further period as the Commissioner allows) and holds acceptable evidence of physical export. Services are zero-rated under section 11A where supplied to a non-resident who is outside New Zealand when the services are performed and the supply is not in connection with NZ land, NZ-situate tangible personal property, or otherwise received in NZ by an NZ-resident recipient. For a cross-border payment gateway service fee, zero-rating can apply when the merchant recipient is a non-resident outside NZ and the service is a section 11A qualifying supply; fees of a non-qualifying or financial-service-only character may be exempt rather than zero-rated.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: New Zealand Customs export declaration (customs export entry)
Bill of Lading or Air Waybill showing physical export from New Zealand
Inward Remittance Certificate (FIRC) or New Zealand bank foreign-currency credit advice for export proceeds
Commercial invoice, sales contract/purchase order evidencing the foreign counter-party
Packing list and port/airport verification records (where goods are shipped)
For services: contract and evidence proving the recipient is a non-resident outside New Zealand at the time of performance
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: New Zealand has no statutory foreign-exchange repatriation deadline for export proceeds; the requirement is evidentiary. If Inland Revenue determines zero-rating is not substantiated, output GST at 15% is reassessed under the Goods and Services Tax Act 1985, with use-of-money interest and shortfall penalties under the Tax Administration Act 1994: 20% for lack of reasonable care, 40% for gross carelessness, and up to 100% for evasion. Fraudulent tax evasion is a criminal offence under section 143 of the Tax Administration Act 1994, and the Commissioner may also issue an amended assessment clawing back the previously returned zero-rated supplies.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Reserve Bank of New Zealand (Te Pūtea Matua), with the Financial Markets Authority for conduct and disclosure and the Department of Internal Affairs for AML/CFT supervisory roles across payment and remittance activities
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: New Zealand operates an open and fully convertible currency regime. The New Zealand dollar (NZD) is freely traded in global foreign exchange markets, and there are no surrender requirements, central bank exchange-control permits, foreign-exchange approval thresholds, or compulsory conversion ratios applicable to current-account trade flows, capital-account investment, dividends, interest, profit repatriation, or merchant settlement funding. The Reserve Bank of New Zealand does not ration foreign currency and would intervene only to smooth disorderly market conditions, not to impede convertibility. A cross-border payment gateway may therefore route USD, EUR, AUD, GBP, or NZD funding without needing a central bank licence solely to access FX. The practical compliance gatekeepers are the Anti-Money Laundering and Countering Financing of Terrorism Act 2009, the Financial Service Providers (Registration and Dispute Resolution) Act 2008, the FMA conduct and disclosure regime, and RBNZ prudential expectations for participant banks. Inbound share subscriptions, outbound beneficiary payments, and profit distributions are not subjected to pre-approval by the Reserve Bank, but each cross-border wire must carry a purpose classification acceptable to the reporting bank. Inland Revenue requires the entity to report taxable income in NZD using acceptable FX rates, and the bank may request quarterly foreign-direct-investment survey data. Overall, convertibility is effectively unlimited, with AML/KYC and corporate documentation forming the real treasury bottleneck.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: There are no statutory export proceeds surrender rules in New Zealand. Exporters and cross-border merchants may retain foreign currency receipts in offshore or onshore accounts indefinitely, convert them to NZD at any commercially determined rate, and use them for any lawful purpose. No mandatory conversion ratio or surrender timeline applies; the only imposed obligations are accurate tax accounting, AML/CFT record retention, and correct reporting of the underlying transaction purpose to the New Zealand bank for RBNZ statistical purposes.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: NZD Capital Escrow Account and USD Operational Settlement Sub-Ledger
NZD Capital Escrow Account and Business Current Account with AUD/EUR/GBP Multi-Currency
NZD Capital Escrow Account and Global Transaction Banking Settlement Account
NZD Capital Escrow Account and Core Operational Currency Account with USD Clearing Capacity

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Fintech EMI viability is high as a treasury overlay but not as a substitute for a licensed New Zealand bank. New Zealand does not issue a dedicated EMI licence comparable to the United Kingdom; instead, an offshore or local fintech must be registered on the Financial Service Providers Register, comply with the AML/CFT Act 2009, and may handle payment processing, FX conversion, and multi-currency sub-ledgering. However, for NZD clearing and settlement through the Reserve Bank Exchange Settlement Account System, the entity must use one of the registered New Zealand banks as the underlying settlement partner. Lawful offshore EMIs are therefore viable for routing card transactions, vendor disbursements, and treasury reporting, but they cannot legally remove the NZ onshore banking relationship and cannot strip the surveillance architecture expected of a High-Risk PSP.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical presence is not statutorily imposed for every director, but practical bank policy for a High-Risk PSP will usually require at least one executive director or senior officer with authority over payment infrastructure to attend a live video interview with the New Zealand relationship and financial-crime teams; a face-to-face meeting at the bank's Auckland or Wellington commercial centre may be required by risk appetite. Remote consular proxy opening is accepted only with an apostilled power of attorney, certified passports and proof of address for affected directors, a valid New Zealand Companies Office certificate, and a board resolution specifically approving the account opening and signatories. No bank is obliged to accept a remote-only file, and compliance sign-off is never automatic for a PSP.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: UBO opacity: Multi-layered shareholding with an offshore trust or holding company concealing the natural persons who control the payment service provider.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: A consolidated UBO diagram showing every intermediate entity to individual natural persons; New Zealand Companies Office registration extracts; audited financial statements for all holding vehicles; personal source-of-wealth and source-of-funds reports for all shareholders holding 25% or more; trust deed and trustee resolution where a trust appears; and signed UBO disclosure undertaking.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-risk PSP scheme: Payment aggregator exposing the bank to unknown sub-merchants, chargebacks, card fraud, and rapid pass-through fund flows.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Merchant onboarding and underwriting manual; approved merchant catalogue and prohibited-business list; PCI DSS Level 1 or 2 attestation; sample merchant files demonstrating customer verification and sanctions screening; daily settlement-ageing model; expected peak and off-peak transaction volumes; and jurisdiction-specific risk matrix for all payment corridors.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unlicensed cross-border activity: No confirmed registration under the Financial Service Providers (Registration and Dispute Resolution) Act 2008, no AML/CFT compliance programme, and no assigned AML/CFT supervisor.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Current Financial Service Providers Register extract; AML/CFT programme implementing risk assessments, CDD, transaction monitoring, and record-keeping; appointment letter and CV of the designated New Zealand compliance officer; independent AML/CFT audit not older than 12 months; certificate of incorporation; constitution; and membership certificate of an approved dispute-resolution scheme.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Sanctions or PEP red flags: Adverse media, politically exposed person connections, or high-risk counterparty traffic through Visa/Mastercard Direct and Fedwire.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Output logs from the sanctions and PEP screening tools, covering OFAC, UN, EU, and NZ sanctions lists; adverse-media investigation memorandum; merchant and sub-merchant watchlist-management procedures; third-party sanctions legal opinion; geographic risk policy; and a standby disclosure protocol for law enforcement and bank requests.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound capital injections should be routed via SWIFT MT103 using the bank's approved foreign-exchange purpose classification for inbound direct investment into New Zealand equity capital. The remitter must be the actual statutory shareholder; third-party wires are not acceptable without proof of agency and economic benefit. The bank will require the New Zealand Companies Office share allotment resolution, an updated share register, an external auditor or chartered accountant capital verification certificate, and a clear narrative in the wire such as Subscription for Ordinary Shares in NZ_LTD. Since no exchange control exists, funds may be credited to the Capital Escrow Account immediately, but disbursement from escrow requires signed bank-approved compliance clearing and matching of the source-of-funds evidence.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound trade and beneficiary disbursements should use SWIFT MT103 for standard cross-border credits, MT700 and MT710 series for commercial letters of credit, and MT400 and MT410 series for documentary collections. Local NZD legs clear through the Reserve Bank Exchange Settlement Account System using bank and branch account numbers; USD high-value legs may use Fedwire through the settlement bank's US routing, while Visa/Mastercard Direct is available for card acquiring and gateway settlement. Every message must include a valid purpose code, an exact NZD or foreign currency amount, and the beneficiary bank's BIC and account details. The bank will screen the payload against sanctions before releasing settlement, and will not send to unlicensed or untraceable shell beneficiaries.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Outright deliverable forward contracts in NZD/USD, NZD/EUR, NZD/AUD, and NZD/GBP for up to 12 months, supported by demonstrated trade, merchant, or remittance exposure

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) only where the offshore counterparty cannot accept physical NZD delivery; because the NZD is fully convertible, onshore suppliers are expected to prefer deliverable forwards, and NDFs must be isolated to specific liquidity-constrained jurisdictions
Cross-currency swaps and rolling month-end swaps for matching the interest-rate and maturity profile of cross-border receivables and FX payables, subject to board-approved counterparty credit limits
Currency options and structured hedging products only under a formal treasury policy with FMA-compliant disclosure and measurement against Value-at-Risk limits

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Return of a New Zealand Limited Company
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registrar of Companies, Companies Office, Ministry of Business, Innovation and Employment (MBIE), New Zealand
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 10 working days after the company's annual return date, normally the anniversary of incorporation; an alternative annual return date may be elected but must remain within 12 months of the previous annual return date
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalty of NZD 157.80 for annual returns received after the 10-working-day deadline; continued non-filing enables the Registrar to give 20 working days' notice of proposed removal under Companies Act 1993 section 318 and, absent objection, the company is struck off and dissolved; directors are also liable to prosecution under section 374(1)(a) with fines up to NZD 10,000.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Audited general purpose financial statements and auditor's report; or, where available, small-company exemption resolution and unaudited financial statements prepared within the statutory window
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registrar of Companies, Companies Office, MBIE; also provided to shareholders and to Financial Markets Authority (FMA) or Reserve Bank of New Zealand (RBNZ) where applicable for licensed payment gateways
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: No later than 5 months after the balance date: a company with a 31 March balance date must file by 31 August in the same year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: No government filing fee; each director may be convicted and fined up to NZD 50,000 for failing to comply with financial statement and audit requirements; persistent non-compliance may be cited by the Registrar in company removal action and by FMA/RBNZ in AML/CFT, licensing or FMC Act enforcement.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual income tax return of the company (IRD form IR4) together with reconciliation of provisional and terminal tax
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: For a standard 31 March balance date, due by 7 July following balance date; extended filing dates may apply where a tax agent holds an extension of time; terminal tax due date is 7 February in the following income year (with possible provisional tax installment alignment)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalty of NZD 250 for the first month and up to NZD 500 where late after one month; late payment interest is imposed on unpaid tax from the terminal tax date at the current IRD prescribed rate, increasing for overdue tax; unpaid PAYE/GST and certain assessed tax may create director personal liability under the Tax Administration Act 1994.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: AML/CFT annual programme attestation and independent AML/CFT compliance audit report (for the licensed cross-border payment service provider/PSP)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Financial Markets Authority (FMA) or Reserve Bank of New Zealand (RBNZ), as AML/CFT supervisor, and any applicable payment licensing authority
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: AML/CFT programme must be kept current at all times; independent audit of the AML/CFT programme at least once every two years, or annually where required by the PSP licence or AML/CFT supervisor for a high-risk cross-border payment gateway; any supervisor-directed annual report is due within the time set by the supervisor
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to maintain an approved AML/CFT programme or obtain independent audit can trigger civil liability under the AML/CFT Act 2009: infringement notices up to NZD 10,000 per contravention, civil penalties, criminal fines for individuals/body corporates, and revocation of the payment service licence; consistent non-compliance may also lead to court-ordered disqualification of directors.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: A New Zealand company has a compulsory independent audit if it is (i) a large company under the Companies Act 1993 size tests applied over two consecutive prior accounting periods - broadly, at least two of: total assets greater than NZD 30 million, total revenue greater than NZD 60 million, or more than 50 full-time-equivalent employees; (ii) publicly accountable, an FMC reporting entity, an issuer, a manager of a registered managed investment scheme, a licensed insurer, a bank, or a non-bank deposit taker; (iii) otherwise required by a payment service provider licence, AML/CFT supervisor, or regulatory condition to have its financial statements or AML/CFT programme audited by an independent qualified CPA; or (iv) not able to access the small/medium company unanimous shareholder exemption. Even below the size tests, a licensed cross-border payment gateway should expect audit as a licence condition due to its banking/AML high-risk tier.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: New Zealand International Financial Reporting Standards (NZ IFRS, Tier 1); NZ IFRS with Reduced Disclosure Regime (Tier 2); New Zealand Accounting Standards for For-profit Entities (NZ AFS, Tier 3); and New Zealand Financial Reporting Standards for small/medium entities (NZ FRS, Tier 4), determined under the External Reporting Board (XRB) Accounting Standards Framework; statutory audits are conducted under International Standards on Auditing (New Zealand) [ISA (NZ)] and applicable XRB pronouncements.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: New Zealand does not maintain a separate 30-day UBO filing at the Companies Office; the annual return serves as the annual shareholder/director confirmation, due within 10 working days after the annual return date. Share transfers must be entered in the Register of Members without undue delay on registration of the transfer and are reflected in the next annual return.
